description: Team SHADOW TECHS is building an offline-first health console for astronauts on deep-space missions. Wearable biosensor data is mapped onto an interactive 3D body map, with instant self-triage guidance when Earth is too far to help. Our team combines full-stack, UI/UX, biomedical data, and aerospace health expertise. Join us in tackling NASA’s Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts challenge!
summary:
AstroVitals is an offline-first health console that gives astronauts instant onboard decision support when Earth is too far away to help. Crew members log daily vitals, explore an interactive body map linked to NASA Human Research Program hazards, and review trends with early-warning forecasts. A deterministic rules engine sets every alert level, a symptom triage tool guides self-care and escalation, and an AI assistant explains results using only the crew’s own data, with an offline fallback. A communications simulation shows how data queues and syncs during delays or blackouts, and red alerts generate a structured Flight Surgeon report with FHIR export. We tested it on 25 analog participants from bed-rest studies.

This addresses the Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts challenge by combining physical monitoring, mental wellness, radiation tracking and actionable guidance in one interface. It matters because on Moon and Mars missions, communication delays of up to 22 minutes make real-time medical support impossible. AstroVitals helps crews detect problems early, act safely and stay autonomous.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

AstroVitals is an offline-first, AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage console built for long-duration space missions. When missions extend beyond Low-Earth Orbit to the Moon or Mars, crews face communication blackouts and one-way light-time delays that prevent real-time Earth consultations. AstroVitals enables onboard physiological monitoring, early anomaly detection, symptom triage, and structured Flight Surgeon handoffs even without an active ground link.

Real NASA Analog Cohort Data & Personalized Baselines: On startup, the backend ingests longitudinal records for 22 participants (Crew A–Crew V) from the UTMB 70-Day Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest Campaign 3 dataset (vitals.json) into both a mission store and a local SQLite database (nasa_hrp_telemetry.db). For each crew member, it computes personalized PRE_TEST mean and standard deviation (SD) baselines across resting heart rate, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, and body temperature, alongside transparently badged simulated streams for glucose, sleep, mood, countermeasure exercise, radiation, and ECLSS cabin telemetry.

Deterministic Rules Engine (“Rules First, AI Second”): Daily 10-indicator check-ins are validated against physiological plausibility bounds, mission-specific thresholds (Bed Rest Analog, ISS, Moon Base, Mars Transit, Mars Surface), personal PRE_TEST deviations (±1.5 SD Watch / ±2.5 SD Alert), multi-day drift streaks, and 14-day z-score anomalies. Only after deterministic rules classify each vital as Green, Yellow, or Red does Gemini AI generate plain-language explanations, non-medical self-care steps, trend narratives, and Flight Surgeon briefs, with automatic deterministic fallbacks offline.

Interactive 3D & 2D Physiological Body Map: Crew and medical personnel can inspect a Three.js WebGL 3D astronaut anatomy (with live heart-rate-driven cardiac pulse animation) or toggle to a 2D schematic across 9 organ systems (brain, eyes, heart, immune, bones, gut, muscles, sleep, metabolic), complete with live ECLSS environmental escalations (high cabin CO₂, elevated radiation/solar flux, fever) and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Five Hazards mappings.

Adaptive Symptom Triage & Clinical Escalation: An 18-symptom orbital catalog paired with 3–5 dynamic follow-up questions factors in red-flag combinations, cabin CO₂, SpO₂, radiation, and active red alerts to classify urgency into four deterministic tiers (Self-Manage, Monitor & Recheck, Contact Flight Surgeon, Emergency), complete with a recheck countdown timer and one-click report attachment.

Mission Replay, Trends, Light-Time Delay Simulation & Standards Export: A Mission Replay Scrubber steps through PRE_TEST, IN_TEST, and POST_TEST mission phases; Trends & Forecast displays 7d, 14d, 30d, and All mission windows with shaded Normal/Watch/Alert bands and 3-day linear regression forecasts; a Ground Link Simulator models Real-time, Delayed, and Offline packet transmission stages; and the Environment console tracks radiation in both mGy/day and mSv, syncs NASA OSDR studies, and exports HL7 FHIR R4 bundles (nasa_hrp_telemetry.json).

What Benefits Does It Have?

Continuous Crew Autonomy During Blackouts: Store-and-forward offline synchronization queues check-ins, triage evaluations, journal logs, alert acknowledgments, and Flight Surgeon reports locally and syncs automatically when comms return.

Zero Hallucinated Medical Alerts: Because deterministic physiological thresholds and SD rules always decide alert severity before AI runs, critical anomalies cannot be downplayed or misclassified by a language model.

Faster Situational Awareness: Readiness summaries (Nominal, Caution, Attention), color-coded 3D/2D body systems, 14-day sparklines, and Real vs. Sim badges surface actionable anomalies at a glance.

Clinical Interoperability: Built-in HL7 FHIR R4 bundle export and structured printable Flight Surgeon reports bridge onboard monitoring with ground medical workflows.

What Is the Intended Impact?

AstroVitals demonstrates how deep-space crews can maintain safe, proactive healthcare autonomy as NASA transitions from ISS orbital operations toward Artemis lunar habitats and multi-year Mars transit missions. By uniting individual longitudinal baselines, habitat ECLSS telemetry, and bounded AI decision support in one resilient interface, the system helps catch subtle deconditioning, sleep/circadian drift, fluid-shift symptoms (such as SANS risk), and radiation exposure trends earlier. This reduces cognitive load on crew members and gives Flight Surgeons concise, standards-compliant clinical context when communication windows open.

Tools, Coding Languages, Software & Data Used

Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, SQL

Frontend Framework & UI: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons, Motion

3D Visualization: Three.js (WebGL OrbitControls, RoomEnvironment PBR lighting, raycasting, live cardiac beat animation)

Backend & Persistence: Node.js 22, Express, built-in node:sqlite (DatabaseSync) for SQLite Campaign 3 & OSDR storage, JSON state persistence, and Service Worker + localStorage offline PWA sync

AI Integration: Google @google/genai SDK (gemini-4-hydrogen) with strict JSON schemas, banned-phrase safety filters, and deterministic offline fallback templates

Datasets & Standards: UTMB Bed Rest Campaign 3 clinical dataset (vitals.json), NASA Human Research Program (HRP) 5 Hazards framework, NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) API integration, and HL7 FHIR R4 JSON observation bundles.

How Is Our Project Creative?

Instead of building another generic wearable chart dashboard or an unrestricted medical chatbot, AstroVitals models the actual physical and environmental constraints of spaceflight:

Every organ system on the 3D anatomical map responds dynamically to both crew biometrics (like live heart rate pulsing the 3D cardiac node) and habitat life-support telemetry (like elevated cabin CO₂ escalating neuro/ocular status).

The Mission Replay Scrubber lets users step day-by-day through real human bed-rest analog phases (PRE_TEST → IN_TEST → POST_TEST) to observe how microgravity-analog unloading shifts personal baselines over time.

The Ground Link & Light-Time Delay Simulator turns communication latency from a hidden concept into an interactive experience, letting operators watch packets progress from Queued → Transmitting → Received by Ground → Reply Received under Earth, Moon, and Mars relay conditions.

Factors Our Team Considered

Clinical Safety & AI Guardrails: Language models must never diagnose conditions, prescribe medications, or override vital thresholds. We enforced deterministic rules/triage classification upstream, prohibited diagnostic/drug phrasing, and ensured every interface carries clear medical disclaimers.

Data Provenance & Transparency: Since real UTMB bed-rest telemetry only includes specific clinical measurements (HR, BP, temperature, weight), we deliberately separated and badged Real clinical rows from Sim supplemental streams (glucose, sleep, mood, radiation, ECLSS) rather than presenting synthetic data as real.

Resilience in Disconnected Environments: Deep-space hardware cannot assume cloud uptime. Every core workflow (check-in validation, anomaly detection, symptom triage, trend math, and report compilation) runs deterministically both on the Express server and locally in the browser offline.

Human Factors & High-Contrast Ergonomics: Designed in a dark mission-control palette with tabular monospace telemetry numbers, large touch/glove-friendly targets (≥ 44px), and an interactive Demo Speed toggle so light-time delays that normally take minutes can still be inspected clearly during live demonstrations.
